headline: Figma's AI agents enter the chat
subheadline: Figma just dropped a live event on co-designing with AI agents, Claude Code keeps shipping MCP improvements, and Lovable went mobile. A meaty week for your stack.

sections.label: Trending
sections.title: Figma May Release: Voice-to-text, question cards, and co-designing with AI agents
sections.description: Figma's May release is a big one for you. Make gets voice-to-text prompts, question cards for better context, version history, and a Zapier connector. But the real headline: they're hosting live demos of product teams co-designing with AI agents — showing how to riff, iterate, and ship with AI inside Figma. Given you're building a Figma MCP + Claude integration for your design system, this is required viewing to see where Figma's own agent story is heading and how it might complement or collide with your approach.

sections.label: Try this tool
sections.title: Lovable launches its vibe-coding app on iOS and Android
sections.description: Lovable now has a mobile app — you can prompt and build apps from your phone. As someone already vibe-coding with Lovable on desktop, this could be genuinely useful for capturing ideas or iterating on prototypes during stroller walks. It launched despite Apple's crackdown on vibe-coding apps, which itself is a signal worth tracking.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Claude Code: Broader MCP handling, plugin support, and environment variable improvements
sections.description: Claude Code has been shipping steadily — the latest updates include broader plugin support, smarter MCP and model handling, terminal/session environment variables, and a wave of fixes for resume, permissions, and MCP login. Since you're actively building with Figma MCP + Claude, the MCP stability improvements and plugin expansion directly affect your workflow. Worth scanning the changelog.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: Cursor May 2026: Security Review agents, SDK in public beta, and MCP support
sections.description: Cursor shipped a Security Review feature (always-on vulnerability scanner for PRs) and, more interestingly for you, the Cursor SDK is now in public beta — letting teams build and deploy custom integrations with MCP support. If you're thinking about connecting your design system tooling more deeply into your coding workflow, this SDK could be a bridge worth exploring.

sections.label: Concept of the day
sections.title: Dreaming in Claude's Managed Agents
sections.description: Anthropic just made 'Dreaming' available in Managed Agents on the Claude Platform. It's a capability where agents can essentially reason, plan, and explore solution spaces before executing — think of it as the agent doing background thinking. No custom build needed; developers can request access. For your MCP integration work, this hints at where Claude agents are heading: less reactive tool-calling, more proactive problem-solving.

sections.label: Read
sections.title: AI in 2026: Five Product Shifts We'll Have to Design For
sections.description: A sharp strategic piece on how AI adoption has moved past model access into product-level design challenges. Covers agent UX, trust patterns, and how digital experiences need to be redesigned — not just augmented. As someone thinking about evolving toward product leadership, this frames the exact conversation you'd want to lead when you're back: what does your product team need to design differently now?

sections.label: Think about this
sections.title: If Figma ships its own AI agents for design systems, what's your MCP integration's unique value?
sections.description: Figma is now demoing teams co-designing with AI agents natively. You're building a Figma MCP + Claude integration for white-label sport apps. This week's a good moment to sharpen your thesis: where does your custom integration do something Figma's built-in agents can't? The answer is probably in your domain-specific design tokens and multi-brand logic — but it's worth pressure-testing.
